title: ACROBAT: Optimizing Auto-batching of Dynamic Deep Learning at Compile Time
problem: Dynamic deep learning workloads have unpredictable batch sizes and tensor shapes at runtime, making it difficult to optimize batching strategies in advance. Compile-time systems struggle to generate efficient batching code without knowing the actual dynamic characteristics.
motivation: Auto-batching can significantly improve throughput and GPU utilization, but current approaches require runtime decisions that miss optimization opportunities that could be determined statically.
method: ACROBAT uses compile-time analysis to profile and optimize auto-batching strategies for dynamic deep learning workloads. The compiler generates specialized code paths that handle dynamic shapes while maintaining batching efficiency. It likely uses shape inference and cost modeling to predict optimal batching decisions before execution.
key_novelty: Compile-time optimization of auto-batching for dynamic deep learning, bridging the gap between static compilation and dynamic runtime behavior.
contributions: Compiler framework for compile-time auto-batching optimization
Techniques for handling dynamic tensor shapes while maintaining batching efficiency
Performance improvements on dynamic deep learning workloads
Integration with existing deep learning compilation pipelines
limitations: Not discussed; analysis based on title only with no abstract provided.
